lines:
## Key Insights

**Engagement is accelerating rapidly.** Monthly watch hours grew from ~10.7K in Jan 2024 to over 1M by May 2026 — a nearly 100x increase, signaling strong adoption and rising per-user consumption.

**Retention needs attention.** A 26.2% churn rate means roughly 1 in 4 subscribers are inactive. With an average completion rate of 65%, there is clear room to improve content stickiness and reduce early drop-off.

## Key Insights

**Drama leads watch hours.** Drama (451K hrs), Comedy (386K), and Action (357K) together account for ~41% of all watch hours across 16 genres. "Gilded Throne" is the standout title with 34.3K hours — 56% more than the second-ranked title.

**Completion rates are remarkably uniform.** All genres fall within a narrow 64.5–66.7% band. Lower-volume genres like Musical (66.7%) and Stand-Up (66.3%) edge out high-volume Drama (64.9%) and Action (64.6%), suggesting that niche content retains viewers slightly better despite fewer total hours.

## Key Insights

**Standard plan leads with balanced distribution.** Standard (5,915) is the most popular plan, followed by Basic with Ads (4,324) and Premium (4,275). The near-even split suggests healthy tier adoption, with potential to upsell Basic subscribers to Premium.

**Subscriber base is geographically concentrated.** The US (3,661) alone accounts for 25% of all subscribers, and the top 10 countries represent ~82% of the total. New signups have grown steadily from ~90/month in 2019 to ~230/month in early 2026, reflecting sustained acquisition momentum.

## Key Insights

**Smart TV and Mobile dominate viewing.** Smart TV (213K sessions, 34%) and Mobile (169K, 27%) together account for 61% of all watch sessions, signaling that large-screen and on-the-go experiences drive the most engagement.

**Subscriber sentiment is strongly positive.** 68% of reviews are positive vs. only 11% negative. Ratings skew high — 4-star is the most common (37%), and 87% of all ratings are 3 stars or above, with just 1.4% giving a 1-star rating.

## Key Insights

**Licensed content dominates the catalog.** Licensed titles (7,034) outnumber originals (1,966) by 3.6x, reflecting heavy reliance on third-party content. The 78/22 licensed-to-original split suggests room to grow original content for platform differentiation.

**Animation delivers the best content ROI.** Animation leads in watch hours per $1K of license spend (0.21), 60% higher than Horror (0.13). With 5,640 licenses facing upcoming expiry, prioritizing renewal of high-ROI genres like Animation and Kids & Family will maximize audience engagement per dollar invested.
